what: The owner's serving rulings of 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02, as the corpus lane distilled them for the website lane (moses-ledgers/frame/SERVING-RULINGS-2026-09-02.md on the private store), written here in the site's own words so a page or a check reads the ruling rather than remembering it. Nothing below is the site's decision; each row names whose it is. Rows recorded after 2026-09-02 carry their own date, and a row that is a lean rather than a ruling says so in `whose` and is not acted on unless it forbids.

rulings.plainly: Serving has one gate: a declared CC-family or public-domain grant. Any language shows, any quality shows, junk shows if it is licensed as such. Language composition, coverage and OCR grade are labels, never gates. The only hold is a licence that is silent or unrecognizable.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: the rights posture of a zone is the gate; every other property of a work prints as a label on its page and on the door

rulings.plainly: The defining sources stay strictly Hebrew and Aramaic, always. A word with no admissible definition sits at its place with no key, in quote form: a finding, not an error.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: the route store admits Hebrew and Aramaic sources only (language-admission-rule-v1); a bare word is drawn bare

rulings.plainly: A licence that covers certain words is usable for those words. Unlicensed or foreign material inside a work is outside the grant, never a veto over the work. Exclusion is at span grain, never by deleting a work.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: a served-in-part work draws its omissions at their own positions, never summarized away

rulings.plainly: Every admissible edition of a work is served under its own name and provenance. There is no canonical text pin. The reader chooses. Differences between editions are published findings, never resolved.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: one zone and one pin per edition; a chooser on the work's address names each edition by coverage, licence family, licensor and provenance; a difference is drawn as a finding

rulings.plainly: The presentation is set by the C0's own language. Hebrew or Aramaic: the full apparatus (cards, keys, lattices, divisions, readings). Any other language: the work presents without the apparatus, a licensed book on a shelf, readable and not interactive. Mixed works: Hebrew spans get the apparatus, foreign spans sit plain at their place.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: a zone declares its presentation class from its text's language; the page draws cards only under HUD_FULL

rulings.plainly: An English translation that rides along with a licence is never the definition layer. English on the card comes only from the readings pipeline over admissible sources. A bundled translation may at most stand as its own plain-text shelf item under its own licence: a book, never a meaning.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: no reading on a card is taken from a translation stream; a translation, if served, is a separate PLAIN_TEXT work

rulings.plainly: Be careful with CC-ND: no exporting it. An ND edition displays verbatim and never exports as an adaptation: no tokenized stream in shipped cargo, no derived artifact distributed.

export_classes.EXPORTABLE: keys, splits and derived layers may leave
export_classes.EXPORTABLE_SA: may leave under share-alike, carrying the SA tag
export_classes.DISPLAY_VERBATIM_ONLY: ND: the verbatim copy with attribution, and the c0-export below, nothing else

rulings.site_reads_it_as: the export gate reads the zone's export class; under DISPLAY_VERBATIM_ONLY the reader's export offers the verbatim text with attribution and licence notice, and no key, split, lattice or reading

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-09-02 (a licence reading, not counsel; the verbatim-file floor remains available)
rulings.plainly: ND may export as (c0 id, surface) pairs in original order, byte-faithful and losslessly reconstructable to the verbatim, with attribution and licence notice: format-shifting is not adaptation. Keys, splits, reissues and lattices never export for ND. Enforcement is mechanical: rejoin the exported surfaces; verbatim bytes back means reproduction, anything else means an adaptation leaked and the gate refuses.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: the c0 export of an ND zone is checked by rejoining its own output against the verbatim before it is offered

rulings.plainly: Material under share-alike leaves carrying the share-alike tag, so what is built on it is bound the same way.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: an export under EXPORTABLE_SA carries the SA licence notice in the exported file itself

rulings.plainly: The collection is all Hebrew text regardless of community, genre or theology. A translation into Hebrew is an edition, never a defining source.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: no work is refused a page for what it is; its labels say what it is

rulings.plainly: No emails, no registrations, no applications, no outreach. A walled resource is recorded as anonymously unreachable, a posture noted, not a gap to fix by contact. The posture is scribal: no name is announced anywhere; incidental discovery triggers no scrubbing panic; the standing hygiene (no personal information on public branches) continues as craft, not fear.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: no personal name, address or account of the owner appears in any artifact this tree publishes

rulings.plainly: A reader's switch may hide spacing (a petuchah or setumah gap) or text about the book (the masorah's own line), never ink of the book. The inverted nun and the paseq are ink: always drawn, no switch. The count is the same either way, since it never included a mark.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: the Marks control at the top of the site carries switches for petuchah, setumah and the masorah line only; every mark is pressable and opens its card

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-09-02, written out in one message
rulings.plainly: The seven demonstrations, each as a rule of the count and the card. Half of the book counts positions. The complex gets the C0; the breakdown happens at the next layer down; the C0 never changes what it displays.

rules.qere_ketiv: One C0 (half of the book counts it as one). The two forms cannot each get a C0; the complex is one card and gets the C0. The C0 displays both forms with their formatting. The card's grouping layer selects between qere and ketiv; the inner lattice holds if either form carries a prefix.
rules.maqaf: Two C0s (half of the book counts two). Each C0 displays as written, the maqaf between them kept; each simply gets its own card because it is its own C0. The inner lattice holds if either carries a prefix. (Revised by the owner the same day from one C0; the Masorah's own word count agrees: Genesis's 17,807 sealed rows plus its 2,946 maqaf joins land on the Masorah's 20,612 within the stream's markup noise, and counting the joins as one lands 2,800 short.)
rules.abbreviation: The abbreviated form is one C0 ON (counted once); the words it stands for get no C0 at all. The C0 displays only the abbreviated form. The grouping layer selects between the abbreviated form and the full words that mean the same, which come from a defining source, never typed; the inner lattice holds if any carries a prefix.
rules.setumah_petuchah: One C0 each, OFF. Each gets a card that says plainly what is going on (this marks where a section ends, does not count as a word, added by the scribes for bookkeeping) and carries the readings, definitions and sources for the Hebrew word naming the mark itself.
rules.inverted_nun: Every word inside gets its own C0 and every C0 its own card. The brackets themselves are pressable too, with a plain line: not a word of the book, and what the mark means. Not toggleable.
rules.half_of_the_book_and_the_masorah_finalis: The scribes' own notes, the half of the book and the end of the book alike, are all included, none left out. Each gets a card with readings, definitions and sources and a plain line. A switch at the top of the site turns these, the setumah and the petuchah on and off.
rules.every_card: Every one of the seven gets a plain English explanation on its card, and every one carries the readings, definitions and sources for the Hebrew word that names it.

rulings.site_reads_it_as: the count is over positions; a complex is one word with one C0 and a grouping layer above its lattice; a mark is a C0 OFF with a card; the marks control carries setumah, petuchah and the scribes' notes

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-09-02, stated; the corpus lane's store still seals two rows (technical frame L4 counts them as one position)
rulings.plainly: One occurrence, one C0. A ketiv-qere site is one word of the book, counted once, whose ink carries both forms in the source's order, with a Q pointer at the site. Two identifiers for one occurrence is a tokenizer's artifact, not a model of the text.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: the zone holds a kq site as one word at one position under kq-rule-v1-both-halves-as-written; where the store still seals two rows the builder pairs them and says so

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-09-03. Stated first: "honest means adhering to THEIR license or attestation"; asked whether public domain by source publication year is their attestation, first "we should retire it, technically books can be rearranged and count as new", then, the same morning, on the argument that a rearranged edition would say so on its own title page and carry its own rights: "ok agreed lets keep them". The retirement stood for one morning on the branch and never reached the live site.
rulings.plainly: The rights the site acts on are the source's own attestation of its rights, carried verbatim; a right the site reasons its way to is a decision of ours, and a decision is the one thing the site does not add. Public domain by source publication year is KEPT on that footing, under one condition: the binding names the printed imprint as the source's own record states it. The year on the title page is the printed edition's own attestation; a rearranged or newly edited text would say so on its title page and in its record and would carry its own rights. A year the site guessed from a catalogue is not an attestation and does not qualify.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: nothing is retired; retired_rights_profiles below stays a list the serve tools read and refuse from, empty until a profile is retired; every binding under a by-source-year profile must carry the year it rests on in its own row; the corpus lane is asked that N carry the imprint (place and year) as the provider's record states it, not a derived year

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-09-13 — stated as current thinking, and acted on because it forbids
rulings.plainly: Not a fan of the Ben Yehuda dictionary's seven volumes at all. No Ben Yehuda dictionary.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: data/ben-yehuda-posture-v1.json declares no served volume, so no entry of that dictionary can be emitted for any volume; the machinery that would have served one is inert and its road is documented as not taken. A lean that FORBIDS is acted on at once; a lean that would permit is not.

rulings.plainly: Project Ben-Yehuda stays, obviously. It is not the dictionary and the ruling above does not touch it.
rulings.site_reads_it_as: nothing in this lane changes: Project Ben-Yehuda is a source of the corpus lane's texts, not a defining source in the route store, and it is named nowhere in the reader's own records

rulings.plainly: Yes Jastrow (2026-09-13). On 2026-10-02, told that serving him means declaring by name that his dictionary answers about Hebrew and Aramaic though his record does not say so, the owner said: "oh ok then yea it sounds fine, both good."
rulings.site_reads_it_as: The owner declares, by name, that Marcus Jastrow's dictionary answers about Hebrew and Aramaic. The declaration admits Jastrow's own m_ids (M12, M39, M49, M65, M75, M106) and no other source: language admission stays affirmative, and the other struck sources stay struck. Jastrow is served from the corpus lane's overlay (r2:mishkan/corpus-lane-builds/moses-jastrow-toggle-v1/, store_version d1a9d6d83c4c), beside the route store and never merged into it, under its own switch, marked rabbinic with each row's year. It starts on and is removable, and its readings always sort below the era's own sources at the same tier, so it never leads a word that has another reading and never lowers a base reading's year or rank.

rulings.whose: owner, 2026-10-02 — a ruling; it replaces the same day's 'not use it at all', which was given while Samaritan was taken to be a script
rulings.plainly: Samaritan is served. Told that the build is the Samaritans' own dictionaries of their Hebrew and Aramaic, kept only where the entry is printed in square letters, the owner said: "oh ok then yea it sounds fine, both good."
rulings.site_reads_it_as: The corpus lane's Samaritan overlay (r2:mishkan/corpus-lane-builds/moses-samaritan-toggle-v1/, store_version 32545d00f4fd, sources MSAM1 to MSAM5) is served beside the route store, never merged into it, under its own switch. Only the lanes the owner has ruled (square_printed, tied) show; the four lanes that wait on the owner's questions stay dark. Whether the switch starts on or off is the serving lane's to set (the owner, 2026-10-02: 'the negative or positive is your layer'): it starts on and is removable, like every other source, and its readings always sort below the era's own sources, so it never leads a word that has another reading.

rulings.plainly: Jastrow and Samaritan are dictionaries like the others: "samaritan just goes in as another of the 36 dictionaries afaik, same for jastrow", and "then we might have a toggle to span across those".
rulings.site_reads_it_as: Each source of the two overlays is a chip on the sources row beside the store's, on unless the reader turns it off, priced and counted per book from data/overlay-book-counts-v1.json; the overlays' own switches are retired, and a reader who had turned one off keeps its chips off. Under the language shelving each overlay is its own shelf, and the shelf's switch turns the whole family off at once. Where their readings sort: like every other dictionary's (overlays-sort-normally).

rulings.plainly: "i wouldnt autosort jastrow or samaritans last, no, just treat them normal, we will add a toggle layer higher up to pull them out as modernity"; and on the order itself: "we dont do blanket oldest first anymore thats a subtoggle".
rulings.site_reads_it_as: An overlay's rows enter a card's pool as rows like the store's: grouped, sorted under whatever order the reader chose, and credited by the same rule as every other record (overlay-rule-v2). The corpus lane's sort_rule on the two overlay indexes ("below every era-appropriate and tradition source") is not applied; a switch that pulls them out as modern is a later layer.

rulings.plainly: "shouldnt it be bundled into 1 pill with 2 M"; and on the corpus lane's ledgers: "it can be yours but his ledgers should still reflect it".
rulings.site_reads_it_as: Two readings are one pill when they print the same: the printed form (the "/" pieces joined, one closing period dropped), lowercased. This is the corpus lane's R pill ledger at its resting position TOGETHER. It holds today for every row the overlays bring, each joining the store's pill that prints the same or a pill of its own. The store's own rows still group on the reading as written, period and all, because the order columns the line reads are baked that way; the store's 7,645 period-split pills join when the bake is remade on the restored shelf. The APART position is a switch not yet built.

rulings.plainly: "1 single hud whereever words happen to match across xyz span. A+...+V"; "AMB / AB / A+B is maqaf specific with AB added from regular megacompspans"; and on the corpus lane's candidate: "can i check it live?"
rulings.site_reads_it_as: The run cards are served from the corpus lane's candidate run-card ledger (moses-maqaf-weld-run-check-v1, strand-run-card, the combination P0 V0 M0 K0 G=BOTH T=ANY O=SEP), projected by tools/project-run-cards-v1.mjs, so the owner can see the card live. A run's whole readings are not in the store yet, so its whole rung says so; the words one by one read as they always did. Which runs count is the owner's ruling on the corpus lane's open questions, and the cards are re-projected when the lane delivers.

rulings.plainly: "lets keep latin negative toggled for now, internal project only"
rulings.site_reads_it_as: Uhlemann 1837 (Latin definitions) rests off on every book until the reader turns it on: data/source-defaults-v1.json names it, and the page adds it to the switched-off sources once per version of that file. Its chip stays on the sources row and says why it rests off; a reader who turns it on keeps it on.

rulings.plainly: "maybe we should only serve as the 39, instead of even having a 24 toggle"; and on a book card: "if i click anywhere i highlighted red it should go into genesis" ... "the hebrew still has to be clickable and attested clickable. and id even make the blue english click into hud"
rulings.site_reads_it_as: The door files the thirty-nine only (tools/door-filing-v1.mjs). A book card opens its book wherever it is pressed, except on its own controls: the Hebrew name and the reading under it open the word card, the attested chip and the license keep their own presses.

rulings.plainly: "we dont do blanket oldest first anymore thats a subtoggle"; and on Daniel 1:2, circling "X common", "puts ~ toshame" and the question mark under its words: "we fixed the errors right? did moses hand you the fixes?"
rulings.site_reads_it_as: Reads first has a position "at this place", the default wherever a book carries the corpus lane piece gloss (relay v59): each word line is what STEP TAHOT gives at that very place, divided and worded as it reads there, and the card opens on it, first and pressed; where no row of the store prints it, it stands as TAHOT own row. Oldest first is one position of the same switch. A headword lookup, a licence preference or the Masorah filter the reader chose still lead; TAHOT switched off gives the word back to oldest first. Pairs keep their own line for now.

rulings.plainly: "the title hebrew blue english is a bit small, attested precollapsed, columns fail, receipts is wordy and even im lost, hightlighting a word is a very dark gold is that ideal?"; "if we need to say the receipts section id put it at the bottom of the book probably ... also the internal language like Y ledger should never appear"
rulings.site_reads_it_as: A book page opens on its title, its common name with the attestation collapsed, the count, and the source as a label and a value in the same columns. How its chapters are numbered is said at the end of the book in plain words, and the build receipts and fingerprints are folded under one press there. Selected text is a pale amber the word reads through.
